newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, seen firmer.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower, seen firmer.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Friday despite stronger-than-expected industrial output growth but dealers said the market could rally next week.
The Nikkei 225 September futures contract settled at 20,535 points, down 135, after touching an early morning high of 20,785.
Dealers said the contract remained well above key support at 20,300/400 and could easily firm again next week.
"There's a bit of a holiday mood today -- ahead of the weekend and with the Hong Kong handover on Monday," said one dealer. "It was an excuse not to do much."
The dealer said the mood was still positive in the wake of Wednesday's Bank of Japan "tankan" survey of Japanese corporate sentiment, which came in far stronger than most economists predicted.
Sentiment was further bolstered by Japanese trade figures for May, which showed industrial production rose a preliminary 3.8 percent month-on-month on a seasonally adjusted basis.
But book-squaring had trimmed some market gains, dealers said. "The market is consolidating," said a Singapore-based futures trader with a commodities house.
The June Taiwan MSCI index rose 2.1 points to end at 389.0 in active trade as dealers rolled June positions into the July contract.
